title: Incremental orders: only what changed since last night

ticket.subject: Stop reloading the whole order history every night
body: The order service now supports `updated_since` (see API.md). Our nightly job still downloads everything, and
the vendor bills us per record.
- next runs: ask only for orders updated since the **watermark**, the latest `updated_at` already in bronze;
- an order that changed replaces its old row (one row per `order_id`).
Run it once today, click **Load day 2** in the Workbench (tomorrow: new orders, some cancelled or delivered),

requires.message: Load day 2 of the API in the Workbench, then run your ingestion again.

acceptance.text: bronze.api_orders_inc holds every order once, in its latest state.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n, count(DISTINCT order_id) AS ids, round(sum(amount), 2) AS total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'cancelled')) AS changed FROM bronze.api_orders_inc
checks.fail: The table does not hold every order once in its latest state.

acceptance.text: The day-2 run asked only for what changed since the watermark.

checks.fail: The day-2 run did not read only the changes since the watermark.

hints: The watermark lives in bronze itself: `bronze.query("SELECT max(updated_at) AS w FROM bronze.api_orders_inc")`. Check `bronze.columns("api_orders_inc")` first: the table does not exist before the first run.
`updated_since` is inclusive (>=): the order at the watermark comes back. A merge on `order_id` makes that harmless.
`bronze.merge("api_orders_inc", rows, key="order_id")` replaces the old row of an updated order; `append` would keep both.
